claims.statement: Kast admits selected guidance and provider resources under its setup lock. CLI-only is the default; explicit MCP adds transport dependencies. Session hooks are passive, and exact legacy registration cleanup follows successful provider setup.
Destructive recovery is restricted to an exact named tree beneath an absolute physically canonical installation directory, rejecting symlinked installation roots and paths outside that ownership.
Legacy installation shutdown fences work, disables the coordinator and retires requests before the selected Host. Managed product fencing is distinct from temporary scoped stop.

Force reset capability constructors are private and their effect transitions consume single-use leases: erasure requires successfully retired QuiescentReset ownership and records the erased fence before issuing its successor.

Control and Host release records, artifacts and installation inputs have independent ownership; fresh installation composes a contract-compatible pair, while Control metadata requires no Host archive.

Control-only upgrade admits the running Host before retiring Control and repeats Host admission after replacement without broker startup. Failure after retirement uses Control recovery and preserves original and recovery failures.

Native installation dispatch binds the sole HOME-derived installation; public uninstall rejects alternate or nonphysical roots before owned removal, preserving the canonical installation and Host files on rejection.

The existing installation and reset effect owners reject symlinked ancestors before directory creation or root detachment; public executable publication separately rejects aliased destination parents before writing.

The retained installed-product fixture stages production Control, receipted Host files and an empty canonical mutation database under an owned HOME before native removal assertions. This legacy fixture does not establish managed-product native qualification.

The opt-in native check uses the sole normal user installation and IDEA profile, requires real compiler queries for C1/P1, C2/P1 and C2/P2, verifies unchanged host identities through Control replacement and unchanged Control through Host installation, then requires original-byte restoration with a fresh Control generation.

The native inventory rejects bounded entry and byte overflow before hashing the crossing input, while runtime installation identity derives from the physical root and ordered immutable payload bytes rather than the archive checksum.

Native restoration retains a possibly unavailable legacy original loaded-version projection but requires private production readiness, matching runtime identity and epoch, and a fresh Control generation; candidate Control status requires verified versions and an admitted live host.

Native evidence preserves each component source revision independently and permits at most three fresh semantic RUNs only for the exact typed MOVED freshness rejection at MODEL_CAPTURE or CONTENT_REVALIDATION with the declared restart_read instruction, retaining every rejection; helper tests cannot establish the live mixed-version proof.

The retained legacy installer offers paired Codex plugin setup and skips it by default for component or stage-only requests. Public product bootstrap instead selects one complete product and leaves harness installation explicit.

The legacy checkout adapter requires selected IDEA JBR Java 25 or newer and exactly one fully quoted JAVA_VERSION declaration before Gradle. Installed native launchers need no JVM setup and pass nonempty HOME and TMPDIR as system properties. This is not a public setup prerequisite.

Full uninstall retains its exterior journal and recovery interpreter/import inventory through cleanup. Provider resources are removed before Host retirement using current provider ownership evidence; conflicts preserve the Host. A registration-lock recheck protects payload removal. Receipt-owned guidance cleanup preserves foreign siblings, and unknown or unsettled state remains protected.

Legacy component candidates retain source-tree reuse proof but are not complete products. The complete-product CI join requires both retained native target inputs from the exact producer attempt without rebuilding; documentation-only validation needs no product candidate.

Developer publication admits the complete retained product and both native target qualifications before promotion. Documentation-only validation publishes nothing. Stable promotion selects exact preview bytes by source tag and record digest without rebuilding.

CI pins BellSoft Liberica NIK 25.0.2+13. The Linux source job and macOS native job configure Gradle cache transport. Pull requests have read-only access, and main push and dispatch runs can write shared entries. Native handoff keeps metrics and finite build outcomes. It produces one unified executable with -Os and transfers its exact bytes. Cache transport alone does not establish a cache hit.
Candidate versions use the CI run number within the installer's 32-bit semantic-version range, while the identity record retains the full run ID and producer attempt.

Host receipt admission qualifies device changes through stable root inode and owner evidence and permits missing recorded entries only for protected removal, while exact reinstall inventory remains necessary.

Legacy installer failure presentation reads bounded stream tails and prioritizes rejection and recovery details. It keeps the child exit status and limits display to 12 details plus one truncation notice; verbose output retains complete streams.

Managed product replacement uses the existing typed replacement journal, immutable installed identity and exact recorded selection. Pending recovery precedes new selection and cannot silently choose another release.

Force retirement admits native worker modes through the shared process adapter, which skips only leading consumed runtime-option families. Management and installer modes remain excluded. Bare -Dfoo, unsupported -X forms, and misplaced selectors remain application data. Unknown modes or unavailable arguments reject before erasure. PID and start identity stay necessary. The native composition case proves retirement of an MCP client with -Xmx256m and removal of disposable Control.

Mac qualification imports the assembled Control archive's executable into the existing publicLauncherTest suite before candidate sealing. The workflow initializes the existing Gradle cache owner before qualification and retains the suite's XML and HTML reports.

The local product gate qualifies clean source under validation-only version 0.0.0 and full commit/tree identity, explicitly fixes component versions, rechecks source after Gradle succeeds, and requires matching staged Control metadata before VALIDATED. Dry-run and rejection cannot claim completed qualification or inherit prior success.

Full and affected source validation and local product qualification request single-use Gradle daemons and keep disk caches. Source validation uses sequential Isolated Projects configuration for graph inspection and task execution. Client cleanup does not establish synchronous daemon retirement.

On graph timeout or cancellation, optional daemon diagnostics bound helper time and output, check invocation association and process start identity before and after attachment, and publish only complete confirmed output without replacing the graph failure or preventing client cleanup.

Routine membership inspection uses separate streamed product and native-input dry-run phases with a default 600-second execution deadline, bounded diagnostics and owned process-group cleanup. Both Gradle commands use two workers, a 5 GiB heap and single-use daemons. Prior success and phase reports are replaced before work; continuation requires successful execution and complete task proofs, while failures and observed cancellation reject with nonzero status.
Managed headless assembly admits pinned inputs and a new owned root, then uses the existing installer with private state. Assembly alone grants no Host readiness.
Whole-plugin exclusions reject unknown IDs, Host roots, and dependencies of kept plugins. The manifest records input digests, component decisions, and exact kept or removed files.
Selected IDEA metadata admission accepts reviewed 262 and 263 release lines while preserving canonical home and executable selection.
Host release assembly packages separate archive and descriptor variants for reviewed IDEA 262 and 263 release lines.
The installed Kast dispatcher exits without local qualification. The manual pre-push mode still starts the full product gate after the cheap checks pass.

The retained standalone archive assembler combines Host, bundled JBR and matching components across its platform matrix. It is not a public installation route or evidence of managed native qualification.

The private setup installation keeps a fixed root identity. Host and lifecycle sockets instead use short HOME-and-target digest paths under canonical /tmp, with owner-private namespace admission independent of installation and workspace path lengths.
The retained private kast-task owner examines retirement before removing its exact shutdown fence; this legacy recovery path is not public managed request admission.

Containers share version-and-platform runtime ZIPs admitted natively using archive and file digests, typed manifest limits and safe paths and links. Payload files and descendant directories are sealed, while the owner-private top-level directory remains writable for atomic rename. Import invokes neither Python nor an archive executable.

Immutable runtime bases bind donor, target, recipe, support inputs and file inventory. Overlay copies verified base bytes, rejects component collisions and verifies base ownership, modes and digests without hard-linking mutable compositions.

InstalledProductSelection admits exact recorded identity for repair without requiring runtime bytes. InstalledProductRuntime additionally admits local runtime bytes for semantic requests without release-server access.

Legacy force uninstall holds an exterior workspace lifetime lease and rejects managed workspace/runtime stores or product-selection.json with MANAGED_STATE_REQUIRES_UNINSTALL before detachment. Managed products use ordinary journaled uninstall.

ProviderRegistration stores only CODEX/COPILOT routing intent before provider mutation. Harness removal forgets only its selected route after verified cleanup. Kotlin schema-2/schema-3 receipts and Python replacement preserve those records without treating them as resource ownership proof.

Control assembly stamps the skill version. Managed ProductInstalled and legacy installation results enter capability-marked guidance refresh; failure or interruption retains HARNESS_REFRESH_REQUIRED, while success clears that notice without discarding other notices. This source contract does not establish live provider success.

Component qualification validates exact runtime, Control and test-native harness inputs and emits COMPONENT_NATIVE evidence before public product installation. ComponentHarness drives compiler and workspace-retirement probes rather than retired public standalone or container commands; this does not grant installed-product acceptance.

The producer records each component-qualified target, seals both exact producer-attempt inputs into an immutable build record, then joins detached installed acceptance receipts without rewriting it. Preview publication and stable promotion require both receipts and retain record and payload bytes.

Public product records require both supported targets and COMPLETE component qualification; sealed-record admission is distinct from later installed-product acceptance and cannot establish native Host success.

Installed acceptance needs an exact retained component-qualified baseline with a successful sealing job, not prior publication or installed acceptance. CI verifies its record digest, source revision and producer attempt; later failure of the overall baseline run does not erase sealing evidence. The baseline can share the candidate source revision, but each native target must have a different actual bundle/runtime/Control composition; metadata-only change or exact repair is insufficient.

Installed-product acceptance checks CLI, MCP, RPC, stop/restart, simultaneous requests across separate roots, edits, different-composition upgrade and uninstall. It preserves private-HOME, foreign-profile, explicit external-Gradle-directory and repository sentinels. A detached receipt is written only after all required cases complete and binds candidate record, target, Control, producer and baseline composition; both target receipts name the same baseline record and source revision. This source contract and decoding do not establish native success.

CI seals both component-qualified native targets before the installed-product matrix, runs acceptance on Linux x86-64 and macOS ARM64, then joins both detached receipts into the retained publication candidate without rewriting the sealed record.

Installed acceptance upgrades the baseline, uninstalls it and installs the candidate afresh before passive discovery and three simultaneous shipped public first queries. Passive calls leave workspace state absent. All three first queries must succeed and share the compiler Host identity of a later query. The receipt inventory requires FRESH_INSTALL, PASSIVE_DISCOVERY and SAME_ROOT_PARALLEL_FIRST_QUERIES.

Uninstall removes only its own unchanged fence before journal commitment and can admit inactive rejected workspace records under exclusive access. Runtime/base repair stages verified replacements in the existing journal, resets damaged owned bytes only after retirement, and resumes interrupted reset without selecting another product.
